title_en: Li Jianqing and Song Baoning v. Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School — dispute over compensation for personal injury

full_text_en:
Li Jianqing and Song Baoning v. Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School — Dispute over Compensation for Personal Injury

Ruling Summary

1. Pursuant to Article 9 of the Measures for Handling Student Injury Accidents formulated by the Ministry of Education, if a student injury accident is caused by a teacher or other staff member of a school physically punishing or covertly physically punishing a student, or by violating work requirements, operating procedures, professional ethics, or other relevant provisions in the course of performing their duties, the school shall bear corresponding liability in accordance with the law.

2. Pursuant to Article 27 of the Regulations on Moral Education in Primary and Secondary Schools, primary and secondary schools shall strictly enforce school discipline, and shall give criticism or disciplinary sanctions to students who seriously violate school discipline based on the severity of their fault, and shall notify the students' parents of the disciplinary sanctions.

Primary and secondary school students are minors whose psychological development is not yet mature, whose capacity to withstand external stimuli is limited, and there are relatively large individual differences among students. As an educational institution, when disciplining a student, the school shall fully consider the student's psychological resilience, and carry out education and counseling work while imposing the sanction. Fundamentally, disciplining a student is also an educational tool, not merely a punishment. Only on the basis of fully considering the psychological quality of the disciplined student and conducting education and counseling tailored to the student's actual situation can the disciplinary tool truly play an educational role and avoid possible tragedies. If, in the process of disciplining, the school merely pursues the timeliness of the sanction without fully considering the student's psychological resilience, and fails to promptly communicate with the parents as required, leaving the parents no opportunity to provide targeted guidance and education to the student, the school shall be at fault for causing the student's injury accident, and it shall be determined that there is a certain causal relationship between the school's violation of regulations and the student's injury accident. The school shall bear compensation liability commensurate with its fault in accordance with the law.

Plaintiffs: Li Jianqing, male, Han ethnicity, 47 years old, Deputy General Manager of the Huanghe Upstream Hydropower Development Co., Ltd., residing at Haixi Road, Xining.

Plaintiff: Song Baoning, female, Han ethnicity, 44 years old, wife of Li Jianqing, employee of Qinghai Transportation Group Company, same address as Li Jianqing.

Defendant: Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School, domiciled at Sujiahewan, Xining.

Legal Representative: Ma Kangbo, Principal of the school.

The plaintiffs, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, filed a lawsuit with the Chengxi District People's Court of Xining, Qinghai Province, against the defendant, Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School (hereinafter referred to as Huangchuan Middle School), for compensation for personal injury.

The plaintiffs, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, alleged: The plaintiffs' son, Li Hui, was a student in Class 6, Senior Year 2 of the defendant, Huangchuan Middle School. On the afternoon of November 8, 2005, Li Hui took a political science test organized by Huangchuan Middle School. The invigilator determined that Li Hui had cheated without sufficient factual basis. The next morning, the relevant department of Huangchuan Middle School, in violation of legal procedures and without investigation or verification, made a decision to impose a demerit record on Li Hui and posted the disciplinary decision on the campus bulletin board. On the same day, Li Hui hanged himself at home. The erroneous disciplinary decision by Huangchuan Middle School caused tremendous mental pressure and serious psychological harm to Li Hui, leading to his suicide. Therefore, the plaintiffs requested the court to order Huangchuan Middle School to pay compensation for death damages of RMB 146,393.40, funeral expenses of RMB 8,614.50, transportation expenses of RMB 10,000, and mental damages of RMB 100,000.

The defendant, Huangchuan Middle School, argued: The plaintiffs' son, Li Hui, violated school discipline, and his act of cheating during the examination was verified to be true. The defendant school, in response to Li Hui's disciplinary violation, imposed an appropriate sanction in accordance with the relevant regulations. Therefore, the defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiffs' claims.

Facts Found at First Instance by the Chengxi District People's Court of Xining:

The plaintiffs' son, Li Hui, was a student in Class 6, Senior Year 2 of the defendant, Huangchuan Middle School. On the afternoon of November 8, 2005, during the political science test organized by Huangchuan Middle School, Li Hui was found by the invigilator to have brought a slip of paper with him and was treated as cheating. The invigilator then handed the slip of paper to the school's Political Education Office. The next morning, the Political Education Office of Huangchuan Middle School, in accordance with the "Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School Regulations on Examination Discipline," imposed a demerit record on Li Hui and posted it publicly. In the afternoon of the same day, Li Hui did not attend the examination and hanged himself at home at approximately 7:00 p.m. The above facts are confirmed by the "Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School Regulations on Examination Discipline," the "Qinghai Huangchuan Middle School Measures for Removal of Student Disciplinary Sanctions," the defendant's "Decision on Handling Li Hui's Examination Discipline Violation," the "Corpse Surface Examination Report" No. (2005) Ning Gong Bei Shi Jian Zi No. 42 issued by the Chengbei Branch of the Xining Public Security Bureau, the meeting minutes of Huangchuan Middle School, the slip of paper used by Li Hui for cheating, and the statements of the parties.

The focus of the dispute in this case was whether the defendant, Huangchuan Middle School, should bear compensation liability for the consequences of the suicide of Li Hui, the son of the plaintiffs, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning.

Reasoning of the First Instance:

The Chengxi District People's Court of Xining held that:

The defendant, Huangchuan Middle School, in accordance with the relevant regulations of the school, imposed a disciplinary sanction on Li Hui, the son of the plaintiffs, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, for his cheating behavior. The act was not improper. Although this disciplinary decision had some flaws, it had no direct causal relationship with Li Hui's hanging himself to death. Therefore, Huangchuan Middle School should not bear compensation liability for the consequences of Li Hui's suicide. The claims of Li Jianqing and Song Baoning lacked a legal basis and were not supported according to law.

Accordingly, the Chengxi District People's Court of Xining, pursuant to Article 40, Paragraph 1, and Article 120, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, on August 1, 2006, rendered the following judgment:

The claims of the plaintiffs, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, were dismissed.

Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Xining Intermediate People's Court of Qinghai Province, requesting the revocation of the first-instance judgment and a new judgment according to law. Their main grounds were: 1. The slip of paper brought by their son Li Hui had no direct relation to the content of the examination; therefore, there would be no act of plagiarism during the examination. The first-instance judgment's finding that the appellee, Huangchuan Middle School, treated Li Hui's behavior as cheating was without factual basis. 2. The act of Huangchuan Middle School in imposing a demerit record on Li Hui and posting the disciplinary decision on the campus bulletin board was arbitrary and illegal. 3. After making the disciplinary decision against Li Hui, Huangchuan Middle School violated relevant regulations and deprived Li Hui of his right to defend himself. 4. In the afternoon after the disciplinary sanction, Li Hui did not attend the examination, and Huangchuan Middle School failed to contact the parents in a timely manner, breaching its duty of reasonable care. 5. In disciplining Li Hui, Huangchuan Middle School handled the matter in a simple and hasty manner, violated work requirements, and did not comply with relevant procedural regulations. 6. The first-instance court found that Li Hui's time of death was around 7:00 p.m. on the day of the incident, whereas the forensic medical examination report issued by the Qinghai Provincial Science and Technology Judicial Appraisal Center determined that Li Hui's time of death was between 12:30 p.m. and 3:30 p.m. on the same day. Therefore, the first-instance judgment's finding on Li Hui's time of death was erroneous. In summary, there was an inevitable causal relationship between Li Hui's death and the erroneous disciplinary decision of Huangchuan Middle School. Huangchuan Middle School should bear compensation liability for its wrongful acts. The first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and incorrect results. The appellants requested a new judgment ordering Huangchuan Middle School to pay compensation for death damages, funeral expenses, and transportation expenses totaling RMB 165,008.

The appellee, Huangchuan Middle School, argued orally that the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct results, and requested the appellate court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Facts Found at Second Instance by the Xining Intermediate People's Court:

The son of the appellants, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, Li Hui, was a student in Class 6, Senior Year 2 of the appellee, Huangchuan Middle School. On the afternoon of November 8, 2005, during the mid-term political science test organized by Huangchuan Middle School, Li Hui brought a slip of paper with him. It was discovered by the invigilator 20 minutes before the end of the examination. The invigilator immediately confiscated the slip of paper and asked Li Hui to submit his paper. The invigilator then submitted the slip of paper and the exam paper to the school's Academic Affairs Office. After discussion with the leaders of the Political Education Office, the Academic Affairs Office determined that Li Hui's cheating was established and decided to impose a demerit record on Li Hui that afternoon. At approximately 9:00 a.m. on November 9, Huangchuan Middle School posted the disciplinary decision concerning Li Hui on the campus bulletin board. Li Hui saw the posted disciplinary decision at around 10:00 a.m. that morning, and his class teacher was also present. Subsequently, Li Hui went to the invigilator and the director of the Political Education Office to request the cancellation of the disciplinary decision, but was refused. At around 12:00 noon, Li Hui returned home and did not go back to school for the English examination scheduled at 2:00 p.m. Li Hui's mother, Song Baoning, arrived home at approximately 5:50 p.m. that afternoon and found the door locked from the inside. When they forcibly opened the door, it was nearly 7:00 p.m. Upon entering, they discovered that Li Hui had hanged himself from the doorknob of the bedroom door using a belt. Family members immediately rushed him to the hospital. By the time he arrived at the hospital, Li Hui had no breathing and all reflexes were absent. The hospital determined that Li Hui had died. It was further found that the Qinghai Provincial Science and Technology Judicial Appraisal Center conducted an autopsy and issued a forensic medical examination report, determining that Li Hui's time of death was between 12:30 p.m. and 3:30 p.m. on November 9.

The focus of the dispute at the second instance remained whether the appellee, Huangchuan Middle School, should bear compensation liability for the consequences of the suicide of Li Hui, the son of the appellants, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning.

Reasoning of the Second Instance:

The Xining Intermediate People's Court held that:

First, the appellee, Huangchuan Middle School, did not act improperly in treating Li Hui's act of bringing a slip of paper during the examination as cheating. Li Hui, as a student of Huangchuan Middle School, clearly knew that bringing a slip of paper was not allowed under examination discipline, yet he still brought a slip of paper containing content related to the examination subject into the examination room. His behavior violated the school's examination discipline. Cheating is an act of disciplinary violation. In an examination, as long as a candidate brings a slip of paper, peeks, or passes a note, it constitutes cheating. It is not a constituent element whether the cheating is successful or whether the content of the slip of paper is related to the test questions. Therefore, Huangchuan Middle School's determination that Li Hui cheated had a sufficient factual basis. In response to Li Hui's disciplinary violation, Huangchuan Middle School's imposition of a demerit record on him for cheating was not improper.

Second, the appellee's act of imposing a demerit record on Li Hui and posting the disciplinary decision within the campus was not illegal. Pursuant to Article 28 of the Education Law of the PRC, a school has the right to reward or discipline students. Article 27 of the Regulations on Moral Education in Primary and Secondary Schools provides that primary and secondary schools shall strictly enforce school discipline, and shall give criticism or disciplinary sanctions to students who seriously violate school discipline based on the severity of their fault, and shall notify the students' parents of the disciplinary sanctions. These provisions do not specify the specific methods of disciplinary sanctions for students who violate discipline. Huangchuan Middle School, in order to rectify examination discipline and increase the severity of punishment, imposed a demerit record on Li Hui. Although this was based on its management needs, it was also within its autonomous rights. Moreover, based on the facts of this case, Li Hui did commit cheating. The disciplinary decision made by Huangchuan Middle School against Li Hui was not improper. Huangchuan Middle School's posting of the disciplinary decision regarding Li Hui within the campus was both a punishment for the offender and a warning to other students. Furthermore, the scope of the posting was limited to the campus itself and was not expanded, nor did it violate the school's examination discipline. Therefore, Huangchuan Middle School's act of posting the disciplinary decision was not improper and was not illegal.

Third, the appellee did not deprive Li Hui of his right to defend himself against the disciplinary decision. After Li Hui saw the disciplinary decision posted by the school, he immediately explained his situation to the class teacher, the invigilator, and the leaders of the Political Education Office, and submitted a request to rescind the disciplinary sanction, thereby exercising his right of defense. Although Huangchuan Middle School did not grant Li Hui's request, this does not equate to the school depriving Li Hui of his right to defend himself. Moreover, Li Hui still had the right to further appeal. Therefore, the appellants' contention that Huangchuan Middle School deprived Li Hui of his right to defend himself was unfounded.

Fourth, after receiving the disciplinary sanction, Li Hui did not attend the examination in the afternoon of the same day. The appellee was not at fault for failing to fulfill its duty of reasonable care in this regard. Li Hui returned home after school at around 12:00 noon, which did not constitute leaving school without authorization. After school, students returning home should be supervised by their parents. For a student who leaves school normally and returns home, the school cannot foresee what danger might occur. Therefore, regarding Li Hui's failure to attend the examination that afternoon, Huangchuan Middle School was not at fault for failing to fulfill its duty of reasonable care.

Fifth, in the process of disciplining Li Hui, the appellee violated work requirements and failed to follow relevant regulations, demonstrating a certain degree of fault. According to the "Measures for Removal of Student Disciplinary Sanctions" formulated by Huangchuan Middle School itself, a disciplinary decision against a student who has violated discipline shall be reported to the school affairs meeting for approval after investigation and verification by the school's Political Education Office. However, before making the disciplinary decision against Li Hui, Huangchuan Middle School neither investigated or verified the matter with Li Hui himself, nor heard Li Hui's statement, nor reported the disciplinary decision to the school affairs meeting for approval. Although Huangchuan Middle School's disciplinary decision regarding Li Hui was essentially not improper, its working method was indeed simple, hasty, and non-standard, and it also violated its own work requirements. Additionally, according to Article 27 of the Regulations on Moral Education in Primary and Secondary Schools, a school shall notify the parents of a student of a disciplinary decision made against the student. Huangchuan Middle School also acknowledged that the formal disciplinary decision of the school was made in triplicate, with one copy kept by the school, one by the class teacher, and one by the parents. However, in this case, Huangchuan Middle School did not timely notify Li Hui's parents of the disciplinary decision. Primary and secondary school students are minors whose psychological development is not yet mature, whose capacity to withstand external stimuli is limited, and there are relatively large individual differences among students. As an educational institution, when disciplining a student, a school must fully consider the student's psychological resilience, and carry out education and counseling work while imposing the sanction. Fundamentally, disciplining a student is also an educational tool, not merely a punishment. Only on the basis of fully considering the psychological quality of the disciplined student and conducting education and counseling tailored to the student's actual situation can the disciplinary tool truly play an educational role and avoid possible tragedies. However, in this case, Huangchuan Middle School merely pursued the timeliness of the sanction without fully considering Li Hui's psychological resilience, and failed to timely notify Li Hui's parents of the disciplinary decision as required. This deprived the parents, who were familiar with and understood Li Hui's personal circumstances, of the opportunity to provide timely guidance and education regarding the problems in Li Hui's personality, thus losing the possibility of avoiding the tragedy in this case. Therefore, Huangchuan Middle School's disciplinary act, which violated work procedures, had a certain causal relationship with Li Hui's death.

Pursuant to Article 9 of the Measures for Handling Student Injury Accidents formulated by the Ministry of Education, if a teacher or other staff member of a school violates work requirements, operating procedures, professional ethics, or other relevant provisions in the course of performing their duties, the school shall bear corresponding compensation liability in accordance with the law. Given that the main reason for the occurrence of the damage in this case was Li Hui's inability to correctly deal with problems and his limited resilience to setbacks, which led to the harmful result, the appellants' contention that the appellee should bear full compensation liability was unfounded. Based on the existence of certain fault in Huangchuan Middle School's working method and operating procedures, it should be ordered to bear 20% of the compensation liability.

With respect to the compensation expenses claimed by the appellants, neither party disputed the calculation method and amount for death damages and funeral expenses, and they should be confirmed. The appellants claimed transportation expenses of RMB 10,000, but the actual receipts provided amounted to RMB 5,463.50. These receipts were all for transportation expenses incurred during the funeral arrangements. Regarding the standard and scope of compensation for transportation expenses, according to Article 22 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Compensation for Personal Injury, the scope of transportation expenses to be calculated is the actual expenses incurred by the victim and necessary accompanying persons for seeking medical treatment or transferring to another hospital. Li Hui was already dead when sent to the hospital, and no further transportation expenses for accompanying, treatment, or hospital transfer were incurred. However, the transportation expenses incurred by his parents in rushing him to the hospital for emergency treatment should be compensated in the amount of RMB 500. The remaining transportation expenses do not fall within the scope of compensation provided by law and are therefore not supported.

In conclusion, the Xining Intermediate People's Court held that the first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and an incorrect result. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, on December 20, 2006, it rendered the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2006) Xi Min Yi Chu Zi No. 267 of the Chengxi District People's Court of Xining was reversed.

2. The appellee, Huangchuan Middle School, shall compensate the appellants, Li Jianqing and Song Baoning, 20% of RMB 155,507.90 (comprising death damages of RMB 146,393.40, funeral expenses of RMB 8,614.50, and transportation expenses of RMB 500), amounting to RMB 31,101.60.

This judgment is final.
